_comment: Run from this package (pnpm --filter <name> run test:mutation); deliberately NOT wired into `test`, so `pnpm -r run test` in CI never pays for it. Pattern copied from packages/gateway. mutate is scoped to the files that are pure logic — normalisation, filtering, splitting, error mapping, parsing. adapter.ts is excluded everywhere: it is I/O orchestration whose tests drive fakes, and mutating it measures the fakes. activity-verifier.ts is the exception, added 2026-10-06: it decides refusals (body bound, error classification, the post-SDK guards) and measured 70.18% while outside the ratchet. Since 2026-10-09 the verifier is split into activity-verifier.ts (orchestration), verifier-contract.ts, sdk-validator.ts, published-key-set.ts, rs256-signature.ts, bounded-stream.ts and error-kind.ts, all in scope, so the split moved no code out of the ratchet. break=92 follows the MEASURED 93.15% (2026-10-08, 817 mutants, after the B-420 test-quality pass; 87.27% before it, and 89.42% on 2026-10-06 with 586 mutants after the unknown-kid budget and its tests; 87.73% earlier that day with 534 mutants; 85.48% on 2026-08-30 before activity-verifier.ts entered scope) with headroom for about nine mutants, because timeouts vary from run to run. It is a ratchet: raise it when the score rises, never lower it to make a red run green under an unchanged scope. Surviving mutants are not accepted silently — each is either killed or written up with its reason. The cross-package map — every baseline, what is excluded from scope and why, and the two shapes of survivor that recur — is in docs/MUTATION.md.
